sight:lore-explorable-home-3.name: A Field Guide to Executive Waterfowl
sight:lore-explorable-home-3.description: The dust jacket promises an indispensable companion for the modern naturalist.

sight:abandoned-factory.name: Abandoned building
sight:abandoned-factory.description: The windows are boarded up. Something inside is still on the clock.

place:ai-lab.name: AI Lab
place:ai-lab.description: A SoMa AI lab with a levitating cortical brain, magnetic containment rings, specimen pods, and humming GPU racks.

actor:ai-lab-recruiter.name: AI Lab recruiter
actor:ai-lab-recruiter.description: A lab recruiter clutching a clipboard labeled “general intelligence.” The entire interview fits in a calculator, which is strictly forbidden.

actor:airship-rental-attendant.name: Airship attendant
actor:airship-rental-attendant.description: A punctual attendant with a brass watch and a very long retrieval cable. Their flight schedule has exactly one departure: whenever you are ready.

sight:shared-airship-rope.name: Airship rope
sight:shared-airship-rope.description: A rope hanging from the airship basket. Climb aboard.

sight:american-industrial-center.name: American Industrial Center
sight:american-industrial-center.description: A brick-and-sawtooth workshop filled with precision tools and the sound of careful metalwork.

actor:industrial-armorer.name: Armorer
actor:industrial-armorer.description: He measures twice, sharpens once, and always checks the paperwork.

sight:personal-b2.name: B-2 Stealth Bomber
sight:personal-b2.description: Your personal flying wing, its dark fuselage disappearing into the hangar’s shadows.

sight:nia.name: Bani · café regular
sight:nia.description: A friendly woman with warm brown skin and dark curls, enjoying her coffee at a table inside Mazarine.

actor:shanghai-bartender.name: Bartender
actor:shanghai-bartender.description: A neighborhood bartender who can measure a pint, a coin, and the precise moment that the floor starts moving.

actor:ssf-battery-seller.name: Battery seller
actor:ssf-battery-seller.description: A local adventurer. Currently undertaking the difficult quest called “one more errand.”

sight:salt-flats.name: Bay Area Salt Flats
sight:salt-flats.description: A patchwork of pink, green, and silver evaporation ponds beside the South Bay. Salt crust rims the water; dirt levees keep your feet dry. A letter-writing desk stands beside the levee.

sight:baybridge.name: Bay Bridge
sight:baybridge.description: The bridge leaves the eastern waterfront for Yerba Buena Island and the East Bay.

sight:bayshore-pocket-garden.name: Bayshore Courtyard
sight:bayshore-pocket-garden.description: A little neighborhood garden: flowering pots, a shaded bench, and a thoroughly unmonetized view.

sight:bayshore-design-studio.name: Bayshore Design Studio
sight:bayshore-design-studio.description: A garden office with recessed glass, redwood sunshades, planted terraces and a carefully fitted stone base.

sight:bayview-common.name: Bayview Common
sight:bayview-common.description: A neighborhood common with shade trees, flower beds, cedar benches, a drinking fountain and paths linking all four sides.

sight:berkeley-esoteric.name: Berkeley Institute for Esoteric Studies
sight:berkeley-esoteric.description: Copper observatories, watchful stained glass, and an armillary instrument of uncertain purpose. A tiny Berkeley campus surrounds the institute: redwoods, a campanile, a colonnaded library, and scholars with impeccable credentials in impossible coincidences. Professor Vale can certify alien evidence.

sight:bicycle.name: Bicycle
sight:bicycle.description: A red city bicycle. Ride it along Market Street and through the park. Press B to ride or park it; dismount automatically at shop doors.

actor:golden-gate-park-bison.name: Bison
actor:golden-gate-park-bison.description: An enormous, shaggy park resident. The haircut is self-maintained.

sight:bolinas.name: Bolinas
sight:bolinas.description: Weathered cottages, a coastal grocer, and a village green among the Marin hills.

actor:bolinas-grocer.name: Bolinas grocer
actor:bolinas-grocer.description: Knows a shortcut. Will probably describe it using a café that closed in 2018.

actor:bolinas-surfer.name: Bolinas surfer
actor:bolinas-surfer.description: Appears to be mentally composing a strongly worded review of the weather.

sight:bottle-post-machine.name: Bottle-post conveyor
sight:bottle-post-machine.description: I never thought about how the technology worked.

actor:twitter-bottle-worker.name: Bottle-post engineer
actor:twitter-bottle-worker.description: A backend engineer with impeccable bottle discipline. Every cork is a deployment.

sight:house-search-7.name: Bread box
sight:house-search-7.description: A familiar bit of household storage, worn smooth by years of use.

sight:painted-bunny.name: Bunny
sight:painted-bunny.description: A very soft Alamo Square resident. Its entire calendar is reserved for snacks and head pats.

sight:academy.name: California Academy of Sciences
sight:academy.description: Rounded green hills form the living roof of the Academy. Skylights, gardens, and the Music Concourse make a small cultural center within the park.

sight:rail-pit.name: California high-speed rail
sight:rail-pit.description: An empty pit. The sign says California high-speed rail.

sight:centeredness-institute.name: California Institute for Consciousness Research
sight:centeredness-institute.description: The California Institute for Consciousness Research. Celestial tiles and a copper observatory promise a rigorous measurement of the ineffable. Professor Meridian still needs a research assistant with a prehensile tail.

sight:center-research-institute.name: California Institute for Consciousness Research · Field Station
sight:center-research-institute.description: The field station of the California Institute for Consciousness Research. Star charts cover the glass roof; its brass instruments are calibrated to a different consensus reality.

actor:captain-ahab.name: Captain Ahab
actor:captain-ahab.description: Carries a reusable bag with the quiet confidence of someone who remembered to bring it.

sight:house-search-1.name: Cedar chest
sight:house-search-1.description: A familiar bit of household storage, worn smooth by years of use.

sight:peninsula-garden-office-69.name: Cedar Design Offices
sight:peninsula-garden-office-69.description: A garden office with recessed glass, redwood sunshades, planted terraces and a carefully fitted stone base.

sight:house-search-3.name: Chest of drawers
sight:house-search-3.description: A familiar bit of household storage, worn smooth by years of use.

sight:chinatown.name: Chinatown
sight:chinatown.description: Red pillars, green roof tiles, and Grant Avenue leading into Chinatown. Keep heading north for City Lights.

sight:cityhall.name: City Hall
sight:cityhall.description: The granite wings and gilded dome of City Hall anchor Civic Center, just west of Market Street.

actor:city-hall-clerk.name: City Hall clerk
actor:city-hall-clerk.description: An unflappable clerk. Her stamp has faced stranger paperwork than this.

place:writing.name: City Lights · Essays
place:writing.description: Pull up a chair. Essays on technology, markets, and the ideas that won't leave you alone.

sight:coit.name: Coit Tower
sight:coit.description: A pale tower above the steep streets of Telegraph Hill. North Beach sits just down the slope.

sight:conservatory.name: Conservatory of Flowers
sight:conservatory.description: A white glasshouse with a central dome, long glazed wings, and bright flower beds. The Panhandle begins a short ride to the east.

sight:cotogna.name: Cotogna
sight:cotogna.description: A brick neighborhood restaurant near Coit Tower. Neighbors eat at a table outside beneath the cotogna sign.

actor:cotogna-chef.name: Cotogna chef
actor:cotogna-chef.description: An immaculate chef with a very tall hat and very exacting standards. Will accept a fish story, but only pays for the fish.

actor:cotogna-diner-2.name: Cotogna diner
actor:cotogna-diner-2.description: A scholar of pasta, conducting an extremely thorough field study.

actor:south-cow-0.name: Cow
actor:south-cow-0.description: A local adventurer. Currently undertaking the difficult quest called “one more errand.”

sight:lost-pirate-wreck.name: Crashed pirate ship
sight:lost-pirate-wreck.description: A tricorn-sized navigational error has become a full-sized shipwreck. The tide has claimed the stern; its captain is still disputing the insurance assessment.

sight:crissy.name: Crissy Field
sight:crissy.description: A low, open meadow beside the bay, below the wooded Presidio. Borrow the windsurf board by the promenade to sail off the beach.

sight:cupertino-orchard-gardens.name: Cupertino Orchard Gardens
sight:cupertino-orchard-gardens.description: Orchard paths, shaded benches and flowering gardens make a quiet circuit around the ring campus. Short courts lead home to low roofs and gardens.

place:etc.name: Curiosity shop
place:etc.description: Other corners of the internet, a past life on the web, and a few digital curiosities.

sight:southern-corner-124.name: Cypress Flowers
sight:southern-corner-124.description: These are for somebody, even if that somebody turns out to be you. The carefully kept storefront has a little terrace and a lived-in upper floor.

actor:southern-corner-124-neighbor.name: Cypress Flowers shopkeeper
actor:southern-corner-124-neighbor.description: A local shopkeeper. The window display changes with the seasons; the welcome does not.

sight:deyoung.name: de Young Museum
sight:deyoung.description: A dark copper museum and a twisted observation tower overlook the Music Concourse. The Academy sits across the plaza.

sight:zoo-deer.name: Deer
sight:zoo-deer.description: Two deer browse peacefully. They have declined to comment on their neighbor’s recent escape.

actor:lucindas-proprietor.name: Deli proprietor
actor:lucindas-proprietor.description: A sandwich artisan whose delivery fleet fits inside the walk-in fridge. The flag is for morale.

actor:dog-pony-administrator.name: Dog and Pony Administrator
actor:dog-pony-administrator.description: A very small impresario with a clipboard, two exceptionally flexible employees, and complete confidence in the programme.

sight:dog-pony-show.name: Dog and Pony Show
sight:dog-pony-show.description: A striped little showground beside Foundry Lane. The dog and pony have rehearsed exactly one trick, and are extremely proud of it.

sight:house-search-2.name: Dog house
sight:house-search-2.description: A familiar bit of household storage, worn smooth by years of use.

actor:pacifica-dog-surf-judge.name: Dog surfing judge
actor:pacifica-dog-surf-judge.description: A local adventurer. Currently undertaking the difficult quest called “one more errand.”

sight:dolores.name: Dolores Park
sight:dolores.description: Palm trees and sloping lawns sit between the Mission and the Castro, with the downtown skyline beyond.

actor:noor-qualia.name: Dr. Noor Qualia
actor:noor-qualia.description: A phenomenologist whose lab notebook contains careful observations, many question marks, and one excellent soup recipe.

sight:duel-arena.name: Duel Arena
sight:duel-arena.description: A tiny garden arena, with a ramp and room for two large financial opinions. Equal coin stakes, explicit agreement, and a fair 50–50 flip. Speak to the referee or challenge another player here.

actor:duel-referee.name: Duel referee
actor:duel-referee.description: An impartial referee carrying one well-balanced coin and absolutely no spreadsheet for predicting which side it will land on.

actor:bolinas-emf-warrior.name: EMF warrior
actor:bolinas-emf-warrior.description: A coastal campaigner surrounded by an agitated chorus of radios.

actor:esoteric-professor.name: Esoteric researcher
actor:esoteric-professor.description: She has impeccable credentials in a field whose existence is fiercely disputed.

sight:fuel-outbound.name: Extortionate Gas Station
sight:fuel-outbound.description: The pump accepts every coin you have. The attendant calls this “market pricing.”

actor:market-farmer-0.name: Farmer Ada
actor:market-farmer-0.description: A farmer in a black coat and tiny dark sunglasses. Can see through the simulation, but still insists on exact change for kale.

actor:market-farmer-1.name: Farmer Lin
actor:market-farmer-1.description: A farmer in a black coat and tiny dark sunglasses. Can see through the simulation, but still insists on exact change for kale.

actor:market-farmer-2.name: Farmer Null
actor:market-farmer-2.description: A farmer in a black coat and tiny dark sunglasses. Can see through the simulation, but still insists on exact change for kale.

actor:market-farmer-3.name: Farmer Root
actor:market-farmer-3.description: A farmer in a black coat and tiny dark sunglasses. Can see through the simulation, but still insists on exact change for kale.

sight:ferrari-car.name: Ferrari
sight:ferrari-car.description: A very fast red Ferrari: twenty times walking speed, with a tank that lasts 56% of the drive to Tahoe.

sight:ferrari-dealer.name: Ferrari Dealership
sight:ferrari-dealer.description: A red Ferrari waits beyond the Bay Bridge. Borrow it for free, drive at twenty times walking speed, and refuel here for free.

sight:ferry.name: Ferry Building
sight:ferry.description: The clock tower at the bay end of Market Street. Watch a streetcar roll past, then follow the waterfront north.

sight:wharf-fishing.name: Fisherman’s Wharf fishing spot
sight:wharf-fishing.description: Small fish gather below the wharf, flickering beneath the surface.

sight:fuel-tahoe.name: Free Gondola Gas
sight:fuel-tahoe.description: Free fuel beside the Tahoe gondola. Fill the tank before driving back to San Francisco.

place:freemasons-guild.name: Freemasons' Guild
place:freemasons-guild.description: A sandstone lodge with a checkerboard floor, brass compasses and an unusually well-funded refreshments committee. Ray, in the red suit, handles admission.

actor:green-banker.name: Friendly banker
actor:green-banker.description: A warm smile, a beautifully organized ledger, and a talent for remembering exactly how you take your coffee. Banking has rarely felt so hospitable.

actor:marin-bear.name: Friendly bear
actor:marin-bear.description: A big bear with small ambitions: sunshine, a nap, and perhaps your sandwich.

actor:ferrari-dealer-attendant.name: Fuel attendant
actor:ferrari-dealer-attendant.description: A pump attendant with a tiny nozzle embroidered on their cap. Their smile depends entirely on how many coins you are carrying.

sight:country-bench-0.name: Garden bench
sight:country-bench-0.description: A cedar bench, made for sitting a while. A very modest antidote to being in a hurry.

sight:peninsula-garden-office-58.name: Garden Studios
sight:peninsula-garden-office-58.description: A garden office with recessed glass, redwood sunshades, planted terraces and a carefully fitted stone base.

sight:zoo-giraffes.name: Giraffes
sight:zoo-giraffes.description: A giraffe surveys the city from an enviable height. Still cannot find affordable housing.

actor:tam-goblin-1.name: Goblin
actor:tam-goblin-1.description: A Mount Tam goblin in heavy boots. The morning fog followed him down from the mountain.

actor:tam-furniture-maker.name: Goblin furniture maker
actor:tam-furniture-maker.description: Mount Tam’s most temperamental modernist. His ball chairs are round; his customer service is pointed.

sight:golden.name: Golden Gate Bridge
sight:golden.description: The orange towers span the Golden Gate between the Presidio and Marin. The Pacific opens to the west; the bay opens to the east.

sight:park.name: Golden Gate Park
sight:park.description: A long green escape on the western side of the city. Winding paths, cypress trees, and a pond full of very opinionated ducks.

sight:lore-explorable-home-7.name: Goose Corp invoice
sight:lore-explorable-home-7.description: The rest of the invoice has been torn off.

sight:gpu-factory.name: GPU Factory
sight:gpu-factory.description: A South Bay chip factory with north-light roof bays, clean-room windows, cooling pipes, and a surprisingly enthusiastic raw-materials department.

actor:gpu-factory-buyer.name: GPU Factory buyer
actor:gpu-factory-buyer.description: A clean-room procurement specialist. Has found a way to expense a trip to the beach.

actor:grain-merchant.name: Grain merchant
actor:grain-merchant.description: A patient keeper of tiny sacks. Every duck in the park considers this person a major philanthropist.

place:green.name: Green Bank
place:green.description: A global financial institution for the people and agents of the future. Speak to the friendly banker inside: deposited coins earn 5% interest per hour. Coffee is on the house.

actor:haberdasher-merchant.name: Haberdasher
actor:haberdasher-merchant.description: A meticulous milliner who can estimate your net worth to the nearest brim. Considers a crown sensible everyday wear.

sight:haberdasher.name: Haberdasher
sight:haberdasher.description: A little hat shop just north of the GPU Factory, with recessed hat displays, a striped canopy, and a projecting top-hat sign.

sight:hiking-supplies.name: Hiker’s supplies
sight:hiking-supplies.description: The summit lift attendant rents skis for one coin. Then ski the winding course and jump its ramps.

actor:hiking-supplier.name: Hiking supplies clerk
actor:hiking-supplier.description: Carries a reusable bag with the quiet confidence of someone who remembered to bring it.

sight:times-square-works.name: Hillsborough Works
sight:times-square-works.description: Two lattice cranes lift the next chapter of the neighborhood. A small fenced digsite, a patient excavator, and Vic’s clipboard keep the main square free for pedestrians.

place:explorable-home-1.name: House
place:explorable-home-1.description: A quiet home, keeping its own hours.

sight:whale-0.name: Humpback whale
sight:whale-0.description: A humpback surfaces in the Pacific, followed by a silver plume of spray. Windsurf into position and jump over its back.

actor:tahoe-giant-1.name: Ice giant
actor:tahoe-giant-1.description: A glacier has stood up, and it is not pleased about your carbon footprint.

sight:illuminati-stairway.name: Illuminati passage
sight:illuminati-stairway.description: A discreet stairway carved beneath the lodge.

sight:in-n-out.name: In-N-Out
sight:in-n-out.description: A double-double beacon beyond the Bay Bridge. The palm trees have excellent taste in roadside stops.

actor:in-n-out-clerk.name: In-N-Out associate
actor:in-n-out-clerk.description: Seems suspiciously well rested for someone living in a city with this much coffee.

place:home.name: John's place
place:home.description: A San Francisco resident, builder, and incurable optimist. Ring the bell and say hello.

actor:square-busker.name: June, street musician
actor:square-busker.description: A street musician playing a song the zoning board has yet to approve.

sight:southern-corner-57.name: Juniper Books
sight:southern-corner-57.description: We organize by the sort of afternoon you would like to have. The carefully kept storefront has a little terrace and a lived-in upper floor.

actor:southern-corner-57-neighbor.name: Juniper Books shopkeeper
actor:southern-corner-57-neighbor.description: A local shopkeeper. The window display changes with the seasons; the welcome does not.

sight:jurassic-biosciences.name: Jurassic Biosciences
sight:jurassic-biosciences.description: A gloriously indiscreet biosciences tower, topped by glass specimen lanterns, a DNA helix and some highly questionable scientific plumbing. A reinforced mesh enclosure stands outside.

actor:jurassic-scientist.name: Jurassic scientist
actor:jurassic-scientist.description: Seems suspiciously well rested for someone living in a city with this much coffee.

actor:pacific-kraken.name: Kraken
actor:pacific-kraken.description: A local adventurer. Currently undertaking the difficult quest called “one more errand.”

sight:merced.name: Lake Merced
sight:merced.description: A freshwater lake near the southwestern edge of the city, south of the Sunset and close to the Pacific.

sight:house-search-4.name: Laundry basket
sight:house-search-4.description: A familiar bit of household storage, worn smooth by years of use.

actor:square-bookseller.name: Leo, bookseller
actor:square-bookseller.description: A bookseller with first editions of books that have not yet been written.

place:limit.name: Limit
place:limit.description: Tools that changed the daily lives of thousands of insurance professionals.

sight:beach-billboard.name: Local Minimum AI billboard
sight:beach-billboard.description: A Local Minimum AI advertisement promises a little gradient descent by the sea. Even the beach has a pitch deck.

actor:south-lost-goblin.name: Lost Goblin
actor:south-lost-goblin.description: A Mount Tam resident who took a wrong turn at the redwoods. He blames the trail signs.

actor:lost-pirate.name: Lost Pirate
actor:lost-pirate.description: He followed the treasure map exactly. Unfortunately, it was a restaurant menu.

sight:lucindas-deli.name: Lucinda’s Deli
sight:lucindas-deli.description: A busy neighborhood deli with a well-used counter and the smell of freshly baked bread.

place:books.name: Main Library · Bookshelf
place:books.description: Fiction and non-fiction that stay with you, long after the last page.

sight:ducks.name: Mallards & ducklings
sight:ducks.description: Mallards and little ducklings paddle around the pond. They seem certain you brought something for them.

sight:marin-bridge-landing.name: Marin Headlands overlook
sight:marin-bridge-landing.description: Across the Golden Gate, the Marin hills look back over the orange towers and San Francisco.

actor:mazarine-clerk.name: Mazarine clerk
actor:mazarine-clerk.description: A local shopkeeper, keeping this corner of the neighborhood busy.

place:links.name: Mazarine Coffee
place:links.description: Coffee on Market Street. Bani is enjoying a table inside Mazarine; browse a few connections to the rest of the internet over coffee.

sight:lore-freemasons-guild.name: Minutes of the Refreshments Committee
sight:lore-freemasons-guild.description: A red ledger rests open beside the lodge’s biscuits.

actor:mira-softmax.name: Mira Softmax
actor:mira-softmax.description: A researcher carrying seven meditation timers, all confidently disagreeing about when the present begins.

actor:square-barista.name: Mira, coffee seller
actor:square-barista.description: A barista measuring the progress of the neighborhood in empty cups.

sight:zoo-motorcycle.name: Motorcycle
sight:zoo-motorcycle.description: A parked motorcycle with a gleaming tank and a neatly printed rental note: “5 coins.”

actor:zoo-motorcycle-clerk.name: Motorcycle rental clerk
actor:zoo-motorcycle-clerk.description: A motorcycle rental clerk with a well-oiled keyring and a remarkably patient smile.

sight:mount-tam-goblins.name: Mount Tam Goblin Town
sight:mount-tam-goblins.description: A muddy path north of the jail leads to the Mount Tam goblins’ settlement. Redwood offcuts, fog jars, and a furniture workshop have made the journey down the mountain.

sight:gondola-base.name: Mountain gondola
sight:gondola-base.description: A gondola climbs the immense mountain above Lake Tahoe.

sight:southern-craft-1.name: Neighborhood garden
sight:southern-craft-1.description: Herringbone paving, flowering pots, a cedar bench, and shade stitched together by the neighbors. A small but very good place to pause.

sight:nightlife.name: Nightlife
sight:nightlife.description: A little nightclub in the South Mission, two blocks north of its former home. Mirror ball, colored dance floor, and two regulars with very firm relationship boundaries.

sight:beach.name: Ocean Beach
sight:beach.description: The long Pacific shoreline beside the Great Highway. Golden Gate Park reaches the beach to the north, and the Sunset stretches inland.

sight:ocean-pocket-garden.name: Ocean Terrace Garden
sight:ocean-pocket-garden.description: A little neighborhood garden: flowering pots, a shaded bench, and a thoroughly unmonetized view.

actor:illuminati-old-man.name: Old Man
actor:illuminati-old-man.description: An Old Man with silver hair, a very discreet lapel pin, and a philanthropic interest in exactly 250,000 of your coins.

sight:lore-explorable-home-1.name: On the Ownership of Ponds
sight:lore-explorable-home-1.description: A slim volume with a surprisingly extensive legal appendix.

sight:oracle.name: Oracle Park
sight:oracle.description: A brick ballpark opens toward McCovey Cove, with green grass, tiered stands, and tall floodlights above the waterfront.

sight:southern-village-gardens.name: Orchard and Foundry Gardens
sight:southern-village-gardens.description: Linked garden courts, tea tables, little bookshops and a birdwatching pergola link a quiet residential neighborhood to the foundry. The institutes sit farther south, beyond the lake and pasture.

actor:tablet-wizard.name: Orin the Wizard
actor:tablet-wizard.description: Appears to be mentally composing a strongly worded review of the weather.

place:orin-house.name: Orin’s house
place:orin-house.description: A quiet Victorian west of Sand Hill Road Capital Partners. Orin sells teleportation tablets inside.

actor:south-grove-outlaw.name: Outlaw
actor:south-grove-outlaw.description: A woodland entrepreneur whose entire business model is your pockets.

sight:pacifica-park.name: Pacifica Commons
sight:pacifica-park.description: Pacifica Commons: a neighborhood green with a fountain, shaded benches, and paths for a very unhurried lap. The ocean air is complimentary.

sight:pacifica-surf.name: Pacifica surfboards
sight:pacifica-surf.description: Bright boards wait on the Pacifica beach. Paddle into the foam lines, press Space to catch a wave, and use 1 / 2 / 3 for an Air 360, kickflip or backflip. U returns to the beach.

sight:painted.name: Painted Ladies
sight:painted.description: A row of colorful Victorian houses overlooking Alamo Square. A good place to pause before riding west to the park.

sight:palace.name: Palace of Fine Arts
sight:palace.description: A sandstone-colored rotunda rises beside a little lagoon. Its dome and colonnade mark the eastern edge of the Presidio and the Marina.

sight:southern-corner-129.name: Palmetto Pottery
sight:southern-corner-129.description: Every mug is a little different. The one with the wobble is about the nature of certainty. The carefully kept storefront has a little terrace and a lived-in upper floor.

actor:southern-corner-129-neighbor.name: Palmetto Pottery shopkeeper
actor:southern-corner-129-neighbor.description: A local shopkeeper. The window display changes with the seasons; the welcome does not.

sight:windmill.name: Park windmill
sight:windmill.description: A timber windmill and flower beds stand near the park’s western end. Beyond the Great Highway, Ocean Beach opens onto the Pacific.

sight:zoo-penguins.name: Penguins
sight:zoo-penguins.description: A committee of penguins, formally dressed for a meeting about fish. The motion passes unanimously.

actor:police.name: Police
actor:police.description: An officer of the law. Their stamina appears to be funded in perpetuity.

actor:twitter-poster.name: Poster
actor:twitter-poster.description: A poster staring into a phone. Someone, somewhere, has made a statement that cannot be allowed to stand.

sight:presidio.name: Presidio · Main Post
sight:presidio.description: Wooded hills give way to a broad parade ground, a flagpole, and rows of red-roof barracks. Trails lead toward Crissy Field, Lovers Lane, and the Golden Gate.

sight:airship.name: Private Jet Terminal
sight:airship.description: The private jet terminal occupies the building east of the runway. Its passenger entrance faces the airship mooring to the north. Click Rent airship or press A nearby; click the ground or minimap to fly, and A returns to the mooring.

actor:ada-meridian.name: Professor Ada Meridian
actor:ada-meridian.description: A director with a chalk-dusted coat and a compass that points toward the nearest open grant application.

actor:elias-index.name: Professor Elias Index
actor:elias-index.description: A professor with a very small ruler and an extraordinarily large jurisdictional dispute.

sight:prometheus.name: Prometheus
sight:prometheus.description: Prometheus lifts an eternal flame over the bay. The fire is for everyone; the birds have interpreted this as including the pedestal.

sight:qualia-bookshop.name: Qualia Books
sight:qualia-bookshop.description: A little bookshop beside the institutes. Its shelves run from practical gardening to deeply impractical theories of mind.

actor:qualia-bookshop-neighbor.name: Qualia Books shopkeeper
actor:qualia-bookshop-neighbor.description: A local shopkeeper. The window display changes with the seasons; the welcome does not.

actor:rail-lunch-worker.name: Rail worker
actor:rail-lunch-worker.description: An excavator operator protecting a sandwich of considerable historical significance.

actor:guild-ray.name: Ray
actor:guild-ray.description: Ray wears a red suit, a brass lapel compass and the serene expression of a man with a very orderly filing cabinet.

actor:software-vendor.name: Redheaded software salesman
actor:software-vendor.description: A redheaded salesman selling the software that sells the software. His business card has a business card.

sight:southern-lake-meadows.name: Redwood Lake and Meadows
sight:southern-lake-meadows.description: A wooded lake, open cow pasture, cottage gardens and colorful city flats along connected neighborhood lanes. The rival consciousness institutes stand side by side on a shared promenade off South Grove Avenue.

sight:redwood-office-court.name: Redwood Office Court

sight:salesforce.name: Salesforce Tower
sight:salesforce.description: Broad glass façades taper toward a flat rooftop and a softly illuminated crown over the dense towers south of Market. The Transamerica Pyramid stands farther north.

actor:salt-conservationist.name: Salt conservationist
actor:salt-conservationist.description: A salt conservationist with muddy boots, a stack of envelopes, and several strongly worded opinions about the phrase vacant land.

sight:zoo.description: A leafy zoo west of Lake Merced. The tiger has excellent stripes and a troubling interest in the gate latch.

actor:sand-hill-partner.description: A venture capitalist who interprets “strong fundamentals” as a personal bench-press record. Their term sheet doubles as a workout plan.

sight:sand-hill-capital.description: A capital firm with immaculate landscaping and some unusually heavy office furniture.

sight:sand-hill-woods.name: Sand Hill Woodland Park
sight:sand-hill-woods.description: A shaded Sand Hill grove of coast live oaks, redwoods, winding paths, and remarkably patient venture capital. The benches have excellent runway.

sight:southern-corner-127.name: Seabreeze Bakery
sight:southern-corner-127.description: The fog is an excellent proving drawer. The sourdough has lived here longer than I have. The carefully kept storefront has a little terrace and a lived-in upper floor.

actor:southern-corner-127-neighbor.name: Seabreeze Bakery shopkeeper
actor:southern-corner-127-neighbor.description: A local shopkeeper. The window display changes with the seasons; the welcome does not.

actor:waterfront-seagull-0.name: Seagull
actor:waterfront-seagull-0.description: A waterfront regular with strong opinions about unattended sandwiches.

actor:secondary-merchant.name: Secondary purchaser
actor:secondary-merchant.description: Their eyes light up at the words “liquid secondary.” Their shoes have already priced in the upside.

sight:sf-fitness.name: SF Fitness
sight:sf-fitness.description: An open-air gym with well-used benches, neatly racked weights, and excellent ventilation.

sight:shanghai-kelly.name: Shanghai Kelly’s
sight:shanghai-kelly.description: A neighborhood bar with a polished counter and a floor that has heard every story.

sight:dolores-skate-dog.name: Skateboarding dog
sight:dolores-skate-dog.description: Four paws, four wheels, and absolutely no municipal skateboarding permit. A very good dog.

actor:summit-lift-attendant.name: Ski lift attendant
actor:summit-lift-attendant.description: An experienced lift attendant in a warm parka. Has witnessed every conceivable interpretation of the phrase last run.

actor:tahoe-giant-0.name: Snow giant
actor:tahoe-giant-0.description: An ancient snowdrift with fists. Its scarf is a small avalanche.

sight:sales-conference.name: Software Sales Conference
sight:sales-conference.description: A red-and-cream circus tent dedicated to selling sales software to people who sell sales software. The ringmaster calls it a pipeline.

actor:software-buyer-1.name: Software salesman
actor:software-buyer-1.description: A conference delegate considering a sales funnel within a sales funnel. The lanyard is doing most of the work.

actor:soren-still.name: Soren Still
actor:soren-still.description: A contemplative fellow taking a very slow walk around the bench he identifies as “compute infrastructure.”

sight:south-cow-pen.name: Southern cow pasture
sight:south-cow-pen.description: Cows graze in an open meadow. They seem entirely unconcerned with the afternoon.

actor:sf-spaceport-attendant.name: SpaceX attendant
actor:sf-spaceport-attendant.description: An attendant with a flight manifest and immaculate coveralls. The clipboard says “Reusable” with a reassuring number of check marks.

sight:sf-spaceport.name: SpaceX spaceport
sight:sf-spaceport.description: A SpaceX reusable rocket and landing pad. Speak to the attendant for a one-coin flight between San Francisco and Tahoe.

actor:square-diner.name: Square Coffee patron
actor:square-diner.description: She came for coffee and stayed to watch an entire neighborhood change its mind.

sight:zoo-monkeys.name: Squirrel monkeys
sight:zoo-monkeys.description: Two squirrel monkeys debate the nature of experience. One has already stolen the footnotes.

sight:illuminati-exit.name: Stairs to the guild
sight:illuminati-exit.description: A long stairway returns to the Freemasons’ Guild above. The public minimap resumes on the surface.

actor:founder-merchant.name: Startup founder
actor:founder-merchant.description: A founder with a pitch deck in one pocket and several possible futures in the other. The vest is pre-revenue.

sight:startup-hq.name: Startup HQ
sight:startup-hq.description: A small startup house on a quiet side lane off the peninsula highway. The orange Y Combinator sign hangs over the door.

actor:times-square-stockbroker.name: Stockbroker
actor:times-square-stockbroker.description: A broker with a pocket watch, a tidy ledger, and an impressive ability to describe a falling number as price discovery.

sight:unlabelled-ground.name: Street / unlabelled scenery
sight:unlabelled-ground.description: Unlabelled scenery uses the ground action menu.

sight:gondola-summit.name: Summit gondola
sight:gondola-summit.description: A gondola climbs the immense mountain above Lake Tahoe.

sight:ski-rental.name: Summit ski rental
sight:ski-rental.description: The summit lift attendant rents skis for one coin. Then ski the winding course and jump its ramps.

sight:sutro.name: Sutro Tower
sight:sutro.description: The red-and-white broadcasting tower rises between Mount Sutro and Twin Peaks. Three splayed legs, triangular crossbeams and slender antenna masts make its unmistakable silhouette above the trees.

sight:tax-hq.name: Tax Authority Headquarters

actor:robotaxi-sales.name: Tesla robotaxi dealer

sight:tesla-robotaxi.name: Tesla robotaxi dealership
sight:tesla-robotaxi.description: A small South Bay showroom of gold autonomous cabs. A showroom attendant has polished every windscreen to a golden shine.

place:press.name: The newsstand

sight:pequod.name: The Pequod
sight:pequod.description: Captain Ahab’s whaling ship. Its timbers smell of salt, tar, and extremely stubborn ambition.

sight:campus-tea-room.name: The Present Tense · Tea Room
sight:campus-tea-room.description: A cedar-and-limestone tea room with a sheltered canopy and outdoor tables. The tea is warm; the discussion is pleasantly inconclusive.

actor:campus-tea-room-neighbor.description: A local shopkeeper. The window display changes with the seasons; the welcome does not.

sight:tiger.name: Tiger

sight:tim-apple-campus.description: A gleaming donut of curved glass and white aluminum, with a real open courtyard and northern gateway.

sight:house-search-8.name: Travelling trunk
sight:house-search-8.description: A familiar bit of household storage, worn smooth by years of use.

sight:peaks.description: The central ridgeline rises between the Sunset and the Castro. Follow the winding trail for a different view of the city.

sight:twitter-hq.description: Messages travel down a conveyor, into bottles and out to sea. The backend is surprisingly wet.

actor:jurassic-raptor.description: Seems suspiciously well rested for someone living in a city with this much coffee.

sight:house-search-6.description: A familiar bit of household storage, worn smooth by years of use.

actor:coit-parrot-0.name: Wild parrot

guild.guildDialogue.node-7.question: Your membership is confirmed. Welcome to the lodge.

start.speaker: npc
start.text: I flew across the country yesterday and complained about the pretzels. Imagine explaining that sentence to someone arriving here by covered wagon. What would impress them first?

choices.text: Crossing the country in an afternoon.
They would complain about the pretzels too.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Exactly! Then I'd ruin it by explaining boarding groups. What modern inconvenience would you defend in front of our wagon friend?

choices.text: Nothing. Let them enjoy the miracle.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Fair. 'Before entering the flying machine, please prove your belt is innocent.' A strange ritual, with a purpose.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: You're right. One uninterrupted afternoon of wonder. I'll keep my pretzel correspondence private.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: Perhaps complaining is our oldest travel technology. What will people complain about on the first moon vacation?

choices.text: The return flight was too short.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Naturally. They put you on the dark side and call it a quiet room.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Finally, an optimist! I'll save you a window seat, assuming we still have windows.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Safe travels. May your next miracle include adequate legroom.

ambient_002_the_sandwich_championship.title: The sandwich championship
ambient_002_the_sandwich_championship.npc_voice: Earnest about a ridiculous ranking system

start.speaker: npc
start.text: Every restaurant near me has four-point-something stars. Apparently everything is excellent, except lunch. Help me settle this: should two sandwich shops have to compete head-to-head?

a.speaker: npc
a.text: A proper bracket! A tiny championship belt for the winner. First judging category?

choices.text: Whether I can afford a second sandwich.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Good. Last time somebody awarded points for exposed brick. The brick was deliciously authentic, but difficult to chew.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: A strong test of repeat business. I'll add a division for sandwiches that leave you financially capable of dinner.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: True. A spicy sandwich and a delicate cucumber sandwich should probably avoid the same weight class. How do we make the comparison fair?

choices.text: Let everyone keep a personal ranking.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Same price, similar food, two recent visits. Look at us, accidentally designing a useful app over lunch.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Beautiful. I can be champion of my own extremely small sandwich jurisdiction.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Enjoy lunch. Please report any promising underdogs.

ambient_003_the_subscription_strainer_co.title: The subscription strainer collection
ambient_003_the_subscription_strainer_co.npc_voice: A recent convert to reading receipts

start.speaker: npc
start.text: I went online for one strainer and bought a pack of three to justify my free-shipping membership. I now strain things at a professional level. What would you cancel first?

a.speaker: npc
a.text: I finally checked what I actually use. Turns out I subscribed to a memory of a good deal. What should replace my shopping habit?

choices.text: Make a list and wait a day.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: I might meet a person! Possibly one willing to sell me a single object. The future is astonishing.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: A cooling-off period for colanders. Sensible. My kitchen has endured enough impulsive infrastructure investment.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: It can be! My friend saves hours on household supplies. How would you tell useful convenience from inertia?

choices.text: Ask whether I would subscribe today.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Actual use instead of imaginary future use. My exercise equipment has requested legal representation.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Ouch. That question just walked into my finances carrying a flashlight.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: If you need a strainer, please ask. Please.

ambient_004_a_very_secure_announcement.title: A very secure announcement
ambient_004_a_very_secure_announcement.npc_voice: Patient enough to have become dangerous

start.speaker: npc
start.text: My bank emailed me to log into its secure message center. I found a coupon for a loan. Was the coupon in danger?

choices.text: Perhaps security is worth the extra steps.
The loan coupon needed witness protection.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Sometimes. But a locked door should protect something. Which message deserves the ceremony?

choices.text: An apology for the extra steps.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Agreed. Give that a careful process. The promotional confetti can arrive by ordinary mail.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: I would log in for that. They could even put the apology behind a second apology.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: It has a new identity and a home in another inbox. What should the notification have said?

choices.text: Just say it is an advertisement.
Let me choose how messages arrive.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Clear labeling! Radical transparency from the people who name fees 'adjustments.'

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Yes. A preference that survives longer than the next redesign would be lovely.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: I'll let you go. No password reset required.

start.speaker: npc
start.text: My ride cost forty-seven coins. The driver said ten reached them. I spent the trip trying to work out what the other thirty-seven were driving. Who would you ask?

choices.text: Could the driver set their own price?

a.speaker: npc
a.text: I'd like that. Insurance, operations, fees, the whole receipt. Which number would you look at first?

choices.text: What it costs to run the service.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Same. A smooth app can make the person doing the work strangely invisible.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Fair. My napkin accounting probably omitted something beyond 'car' and 'very confident logo.'

b.speaker: npc
b.text: Interesting. A little more bargaining, a little less mystery. Would you prefer that?

choices.text: Yes, if I saw the price up front.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: An agreement between two people! It sounds almost historical.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Convenience has value. I'd just like its price to introduce itself honestly.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Hope your next ride arrives promptly and pays everybody properly.

ambient_006_the_blue_bird_committee.title: The blue bird committee
ambient_006_the_blue_bird_committee.npc_voice: Newly enthusiastic about a tiny discovery

start.speaker: npc
start.text: I used to think birdwatching sounded dull. Then one absurdly blue bird crossed my path and I followed it for twenty minutes. Have you had a hobby sneak up on you?

choices.text: I would rather just enjoy the walk.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Excellent. Our club currently has one member and no idea what that bird was. How shall we identify it?

choices.text: Listen and watch for a while.
Give it a ridiculous temporary name.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: A field method! I'll put my phone away. We can be confused at a much more peaceful pace.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Professor Blue Jacket it is. Taxonomy can catch up with us later.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: Entirely fair. Do you think naming everything helps us notice it, or gets in the way?

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Then the next walk becomes a reunion. That's a lovely way to build a neighborhood.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: I'll let the bird remain a small blue mystery. It has not requested our paperwork.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: If you see Professor Blue Jacket, tell them the committee was impressed.

ambient_007_the_party_badge_problem.title: The party badge problem
ambient_007_the_party_badge_problem.npc_voice: A little starstruck, aware of it

start.speaker: npc
start.text: At that party I kept meeting people from the same impressive lab. By the third introduction I was nodding before they said anything. What should I ask next time?

choices.text: Ask what they actually enjoy working on.
Ask everyone the same silly question.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Good. Something a badge can't answer. What if the answer gets very technical?

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: A real conversation instead of an exchange of prestigious rectangles. I could manage that.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Then we both get to relax. Perhaps an excellent researcher can survive one ordinary question.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: A control group! What question cuts through a room full of impressive employers?

choices.text: What is your most useless talent?
What did you change your mind about?

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Perfect. Tonight's keynote is now competitive napkin folding.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Ooh. That might tell me more than the biography. I'll save it for after the snack table.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Enjoy the party. The cheese has no institutional affiliation.

ambient_008_the_bedroom_data_center.title: The bedroom data center
ambient_008_the_bedroom_data_center.npc_voice: Smug, but prepared to laugh at it

start.speaker: npc
start.text: The big cloud services went down and my bedroom server stayed up. I enjoyed eight magnificent minutes of superiority. Then its fan kept me awake. Would you run your own?

choices.text: Yes. I like controlling my tools.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: There's real satisfaction in it. What would you host first?

choices.text: Something small that I can repair.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Wise. My first plan was 'everything,' which is a poor incident-response strategy.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Finally, infrastructure with a mission. We must not lose the one where the cat looks like an accountant.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: Valid. Somebody still has to do the maintenance. What would persuade you?

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: That's the best reason. The bragging window is short, but the education sticks around.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Yes. The ultimate technical specification: does not sound like a hair dryer at midnight.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: I'll see you at the next outage. Or the hardware store.

ambient_009_thirty_five_seconds_of_spinn.title: Thirty-five seconds of spinning
ambient_009_thirty_five_seconds_of_spinn.npc_voice: Offended on behalf of everyone's afternoon

start.speaker: npc
start.text: I waited through a thirty-five-second loading animation just to download my bill. I could have drawn the bill faster. What should happen when a website wastes your time?

choices.text: The designers should have to use it.
Maybe there is a hard technical problem.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: On a slow phone, at the end of a long day. What task would you assign them?

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Exactly. No guided demo. Let the download button defend itself.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: A challenging final exam. We might need to bring snacks and an advocate.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: There might be. I'd be less annoyed if it told me what was happening. What would help?

choices.text: Let me do something else meanwhile.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: 'Finding your bill' beats a spinning wheel performing interpretive dance.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Yes. Waiting feels different when it doesn't hold your whole afternoon hostage.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: You've been much quicker than the spinner. Thank you.

ambient_010_the_pamphlet_that_picked_a_f.title: The pamphlet that picked a fight
ambient_010_the_pamphlet_that_picked_a_f.npc_voice: Skeptical without wanting a shouting match

start.speaker: npc
start.text: This pamphlet says everything is broken and sounds thrilled about it. I can't tell whether it explains anything. How do you judge a wonderfully angry writer?

choices.text: Ask them to make the argument plainly.
Sometimes anger notices a real problem.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Yes. Let the idea stand without the dramatic lighting. What would count as a good answer?

choices.text: A claim I could actually check.
A fair account of the other side.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: A welcome change from being told that everyone who disagrees is asleep.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: That would impress me. A rival who can speak in full sentences is much harder to defeat.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: Certainly. A smoke alarm can be useful even if it sings badly. What comes after the alarm?

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Good. I have room for one more idea and absolutely no room for another apocalypse-themed newsletter.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: I'll accept that. Being dissatisfied is a beginning, not a finished reading list.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Take care. I hope your next pamphlet has both passion and footnotes.

ambient_011_the_suspicious_philosopher.title: The suspicious philosopher
ambient_011_the_suspicious_philosopher.npc_voice: A reader with a detective streak

start.speaker: npc
start.text: I bought an introduction to philosophy. The author has published forty-seven books this month, and the cover has six fingers. Where would you start the investigation?

choices.text: Find out whether the author exists.
Can a generated book still be useful?

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Their biography says 'a passionate lifelong explorer of wisdom.' I could write that about a confused pigeon. What would convince you?

choices.text: Read a few pages and judge those.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Good. Evidence gets a chair; atmospheric adjectives can stand outside.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Fair. A real name can write nonsense too. The prose should do some actual thinking.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: It might, if someone checks it and tells you what it is. What bothers you more?

choices.text: Pretending there was a human expert.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Same. I bought someone's understanding and received an unexplained assembly process.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Yes. Every fake shortcut makes the good books harder to find. The shelf starts charging an attention tax.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: May your next author have a bibliography and the standard number of hands.

ambient_012_the_snack_time_exchange_rate.title: The snack-time exchange rate
ambient_012_the_snack_time_exchange_rate.npc_voice: Amused by the body's inconvenient bookkeeping

start.speaker: npc
start.text: I can eat a snack in thirty seconds and spend ages walking around afterward. My body has a very strange exchange rate. Would you rather take a long walk or sit somewhere with a really good snack?

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Good choice. I enjoy movement much more when it's a destination instead of a punishment. Where are we going?

choices.text: Somewhere with a snack at the end.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Excellent. Trees do not display a leaderboard, and I appreciate that.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: An itinerary! Exercise and pleasure have agreed to share a calendar.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: I respect an honest agenda. Can I persuade you to take it outside?

choices.text: Only if you stop doing snack mathematics.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Then we've improved the day without turning lunch into a moral tribunal.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Deal. The spreadsheet is closed. Tell me whether it's crunchy.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Enjoy your afternoon. You don't owe me an exercise report.

start.speaker: npc
start.text: This refill soap is so thin it has nearly become a beverage. Same label, different seller. How would you decide whether to trust the next bottle?

choices.text: Buy from a seller I can identify.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: That would help. I want to know who to ask when my soap develops a new personality. What matters most?

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Yes. A chain of responsibility shorter than a detective novel.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Agreed. A guarantee becomes more convincing when it survives contact with an actual complaint.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: Possible. I'm annoyed, not a laboratory. How would you check before accusing anyone?

choices.text: Ask the maker about the batch.
Compare it with a known bottle.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Sensible. Evidence before the furious review. I shall attempt this advanced emotional technology.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Good. Two bottles, one sink, and perhaps a conclusive bubble.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Stay clean. Ideally with something capable of producing foam.

ambient_014_the_seven_ticket_mystery.title: The seven-ticket mystery
ambient_014_the_seven_ticket_mystery.npc_voice: Enjoys a disagreement that can stay civil

start.speaker: npc
start.text: A driver told me the speed cameras were unfair. They'd collected seven tickets. I was trying to look sympathetic while thinking about the crosswalk. Where would you start?

choices.text: With the people trying to cross.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Same. A street should be usable without rehearsing a sprint. What would make enforcement feel fair?

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Yes. The rule should be something drivers can follow before receiving an expensive souvenir.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Absolutely. A camera can be useful without becoming infallible by decree.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: Good point. A road that invites racing and a sign asking nicely are having different conversations. What would you change?

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Something you can feel through the steering wheel. Better than asking paint to do all the work.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Yes. Success should mean fewer frightened crossings, not an impressive stack of fines.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: See you around. I'll be crossing with the signal, at a dignified pace.

ambient_015_a_conversation_about_tools.title: A conversation about tools
ambient_015_a_conversation_about_tools.npc_voice: A tired interviewer trying to stay fair

start.speaker: npc
start.text: I've heard the same polished interview answer so often I can recite it backward. I want to know whether someone enjoys understanding their tools. What would you ask?

choices.text: Ask about a bug they actually solved.
Trivia can reject perfectly good people.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Good. A story with dirt on its shoes. What follow-up would reveal real understanding?

choices.text: What did they try that failed?
Ask them to explain it simply.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Exactly. A genuine dead end usually tells you more than a perfect victory lap.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Yes. If the explanation needs a fog machine, we may need another question.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: That's fair. Hiring is a narrow window into a whole person. What would make the window better?

choices.text: Let them work through a small problem.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: And ask questions while they do it. I'd rather see thinking than a recital.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: A useful invitation. Curiosity has more than one accent, and I should remember that.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Thanks. You've improved the interview without even applying.

start.speaker: npc
start.text: My phone fixes words I meant to write and leaves the obvious typos alone. It recently corrected my compliment into an insult. Should I apologize, or blame the device?

a.speaker: npc
a.text: A balanced statement: personal responsibility followed by a small prosecution. What should the apology say?

choices.text: My phone has become my enemy.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Clean, direct, humane. The keyboard will hate it.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Accurate, but now they'll ask about your phone instead of accepting the compliment. It has stolen the conversation too.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: A bold return to sound. What if the dictation mangles that as well?

choices.text: Meet them and say it in person.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Ah. The original codec. Perhaps we were too quick to discard it.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: No update required, though I might still stumble over the sentence on my own.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Go forth. May your next message remain the one you wrote.

ambient_017_the_impeccable_paper_person.title: The impeccable paper person
ambient_017_the_impeccable_paper_person.npc_voice: Courteous, with an increasingly raised eyebrow

start.speaker: npc
start.text: A candidate sent a glittering résumé and a strangely convincing pile of paperwork. The career began in a fancy lab; the answers sounded like a sales pitch. What would you verify first?

choices.text: Do not confuse nervousness with dishonesty.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Yes. A famous employer tells me where someone sat, not what they did. How would you keep it fair?

choices.text: Ask the same questions of everyone.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: A working example beats a wall of logos. Even a small project can have a real author.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Exactly. Suspicion should lead to a consistent process, not a talent show for my prejudices.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: Thank you. A quiet person can be excellent at work and dreadful at interviews. What would give them room?

choices.text: Verify references without making a scene.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Good. Actual work contains questions. We should probably allow them in the audition.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Calm and specific. My inner detective can put the enormous hat away.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Take care. I hope your next introduction requires less detective work.

start.speaker: npc
start.text: I'm starting a company with a target market of the entire galaxy. We have no product, but the investor presentation includes several planets. What should I put on slide two?

a.speaker: npc
a.text: A brave constraint. Apparently Jupiter has been difficult to schedule. What should I ask our first Earth customer?

choices.text: What problem do you need solved?

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: That might require changing the pitch. Terrifying. Promising, too.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: A famously dangerous question for a slide deck. I'll leave space for the answer.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: You've seen through me. The founders' lounge is currently our only profitable customer segment. What would make you trust us?

choices.text: Commit to building before cashing out.
Show what the team has delivered.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Reasonable. Perhaps the spaceship should exist before I choose its private dining room.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Actual progress. Dreadful for the animations budget, excellent for the company.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Keep looking up. Please do not count the stars as confirmed customers.

ambient_019_fame_before_revenue.title: Fame before revenue
ambient_019_fame_before_revenue.npc_voice: Sympathetic to dreamers, suspicious of applause

start.speaker: npc
start.text: My friend makes excellent things quietly. Another friend has a famous startup that mostly makes announcements. Guess which one gets invited to speak?

choices.text: Maybe they both deserve a little attention.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Naturally. Still, telling a story can help people attempt something difficult. When does that become worthwhile?

choices.text: When it helps other people try.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: A promise with a delivery date. I can applaud that without needing a smoke machine.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: True. Courage can be contagious. I'd like the inspiration to outlive the launch party.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: That's generous. What would you ask each of them at dinner?

choices.text: What are you proud of making?
What was harder than you expected?

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Good. A question that welcomes a useful tool and a sincere attempt.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: An excellent equalizer. Even our keynote speaker must occasionally confront a printer.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: If you make something quietly today, consider this a small round of applause.

ambient_020_the_banker_who_answers.title: The banker who answers
ambient_020_the_banker_who_answers.npc_voice: Pleasantly surprised by an old-fashioned solution

start.speaker: npc
start.text: My old bank had a maze of online forms. My new banker just asks what I need and calls to confirm. Has software ever made something harder than asking a person?

choices.text: A good form can be faster than a person.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: A portal is such an ambitious name for a locked cupboard. What would your ideal version do?

choices.text: Let me describe the problem in my own words.
Get a human when the form fails.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Yes. Start with the problem I have, rather than the menu they expected me to need.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: A graceful escape hatch. Civilization occasionally fits inside one button.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: Absolutely. I'd like the right tool for each job. Which task should stay simple and self-service?

choices.text: The thing I do every week.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Precisely. Save the conversation for the strange cases. Don't make my rent payment a relationship exercise.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Then I know what happened and can get on with my day. A surprisingly ambitious product goal.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Thanks for the conversation. No ticket number has been created.

start.speaker: npc
start.text: Our neighborhood meeting spent two hours on the most divisive proposal and never reached the broken crossing light. If you had one hour of everyone's goodwill, what would you spend it on?

choices.text: One useful thing we can agree on.
The difficult issue might matter most.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: A crossing light feels achievable. But how do we avoid postponing every hard question forever?

choices.text: Put the hard question on a real schedule.
Make the small win build trust.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Good. 'Later' should have a date, not a permanent apartment in the minutes.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Yes. It is easier to disagree after discovering the other person also wants children to cross safely.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: Fair. Sometimes the awkward subject is the important one. How would you keep the room listening?

choices.text: Agree on what success would look like.
Ask people what they are afraid of.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: We might discover we want similar things and have been fighting over the route.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: A better opening than accusing them of enjoying broken traffic lights.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Wish us luck. I've brought a watch and an unreasonable hope of finishing on time.

ambient_022_the_office_museum.title: The office museum
ambient_022_the_office_museum.npc_voice: Fond of the past without wanting to live there

start.speaker: npc
start.text: I found our old office's ping-pong paddles. The new office has a wall about relentless optimization. Which artifact belongs in the museum?

choices.text: The wall. Nobody can optimize forever.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Maybe. Though a fun office could still be a terrible job. What perk would you actually keep?

choices.text: Time to have a life outside it.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: A benefit too large to fit on the snack shelf. I'd take it.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Yes. Hard to photograph for recruiting, much easier to appreciate at six on a difficult evening.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: I'm considering hanging it sideways and calling it a wellness intervention. What would you measure instead?

choices.text: Whether people can sustain the pace.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: A refreshingly concrete hobby for a workplace.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Right. A sprint is impressive; making everyone pretend the sprint is a lifestyle gets strange.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Take a paddle if you like. Its quarterly targets are very reasonable.

ambient_023_the_streetlight_repair_econo.title: The streetlight repair economy
ambient_023_the_streetlight_repair_econo.npc_voice: Concerned about the street, bored by excuses

start.speaker: npc
start.text: Our streetlight lost a small bit of metal and now needs a very large repair budget. Everyone can quote the cost; nobody can tell me when the street will be bright. What would you ask?

choices.text: How do we prevent the next repair?
Who is responsible for the result?

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Exactly. I want the lamp to illuminate the pavement, not a permanent business opportunity. Where would you start?

choices.text: Find out why the material keeps disappearing.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: A small trial, measured honestly. Much cheaper than announcing that the problem has become traditional.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Follow the actual chain of events. Better than treating every dark street as a fresh surprise.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: That question causes extraordinary shuffling of papers. What result should they report?

choices.text: How long the lights actually stay on.
The full cost to the neighborhood.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Perfect. A number that includes the street instead of merely the invoices.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Yes. Repairs cost money; darkness costs people their evening walk. The spreadsheet should notice both.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Here's hoping the next time we meet, I can actually see your face.

ambient_024_the_armchair_civic_warrior.title: The armchair civic warrior
ambient_024_the_armchair_civic_warrior.npc_voice: Loves the city and knows their own excuses

start.speaker: npc
start.text: I told my partner I'd fight for this city. They asked whether that meant attending a meeting or posting angrily from the sofa. Brutal question. What counts as showing up?

choices.text: Do one small thing in person.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: All right. No heroic soundtrack. What should I try?

choices.text: Go to the meeting and listen.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: A visible result and perhaps a new neighbor. My sofa will endure my absence.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: A difficult first mission for someone with so many opinions. Probably a useful one.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: True. Sometimes a clear explanation reaches people. How would I know I'm contributing rather than just venting?

choices.text: Give readers an action they can take.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Something beyond 'be as annoyed as me.' I can work on that.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Ouch. An excellent standard. I'll start by asking a question I don't already know my answer to.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: See you out there. Ideally somewhere beyond my own comment section.

ambient_025_the_retired_rebel.title: The retired rebel
ambient_025_the_retired_rebel.npc_voice: Amused by their own outdated pose

start.speaker: npc
start.text: An old friend built their whole identity around breaking a rule. Then the rule changed. Now they're an ordinary customer with rebellious stationery. Where does a rebel go next?

choices.text: Enjoy winning and find a new hobby.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: That would be more useful than defending the jacket. What makes a cause worth it?

choices.text: Whether I would care without an audience.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: A sturdier foundation than whether it annoys somebody at dinner.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: An uncomfortable test. Several of my opinions have just gone very quiet.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: A surprisingly neglected option! What hobby suits a former outlaw?

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Excellent. Fight the bindweed. It never acknowledges your victories.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Radical. No manifesto, no branding, just a sandwich eaten in peace.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Take care. You're allowed to grow beyond your favorite argument.

ambient_026_the_golden_goose_committee.title: The golden goose committee
ambient_026_the_golden_goose_committee.npc_voice: A practical caretaker of an elaborate metaphor

start.speaker: npc
start.text: Imagine our town has one goose laying golden eggs. Everyone agrees it should help fund the town, then argues about feathers. What's the first rule of goose policy?

choices.text: Find out whether there really is only one goose.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Sensible. But the town needs roads, schools, and somewhere for the goose keeper to live. How do you settle that?

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Yes. A brilliant plan for this afternoon can be a terrible plan for next spring.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Then both the town and the goose can plan. Even metaphors benefit from clear rules.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: Excellent question. A fragile town should probably grow more ways to prosper. What would you invest in?

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: More people able to build something worthwhile. A less dramatic story, and perhaps a better town.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: A good road rarely gets the keynote speech. The geese still need it.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Thanks. I'll spare you the committee's eighty-page appendix on nesting incentives.

ambient_027_the_lucky_crook_portfolio.title: The lucky crook portfolio
ambient_027_the_lucky_crook_portfolio.npc_voice: Firm about fairness, gentle with the listener

start.speaker: npc
start.text: Someone at dinner praised a fictional swindler for making one spectacular investment with stolen deposits. Would you call that skill?

choices.text: Luck does not make the theft clever.
There might be skill mixed in with wrongdoing.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Right. You can win a race after borrowing everyone else's bicycle without asking. What should we judge?

choices.text: The whole record, including the losses.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: And whether the people supplying it ever agreed to the risk. The winning ticket doesn't erase that.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Exactly. A highlight reel can turn almost any disaster into a keynote.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: Possibly. We can acknowledge an ability without handing back everyone's trust. What would rebuilding trust require?

choices.text: A lot more than one good prediction.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Actual repair. Much harder than a comeback interview with flattering lighting.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Yes. Trust grows from repeated honest choices, especially when honesty is inconvenient.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: May your brilliant opportunities include permission from the people funding them.

start.speaker: npc
start.text: In the city I debate tasting menus. Visiting family, I eat potatoes with salt and think they're marvelous. Has my palate been lying to me?

choices.text: Maybe the potatoes are just very good.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: I think so. A familiar kitchen does extraordinary things to an ordinary potato. What would you bring to that table?

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Then dinner comes with a story instead of a sales description.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Lovely. Tradition can make room for a guest without losing its chair.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: An agricultural explanation! What would be your test of an excellent meal?

choices.text: Would I want it again tomorrow?
Can I enjoy it without describing it?

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: A strong standard. Several prestigious foams have failed it immediately.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Yes. Dinner can survive without becoming content.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Enjoy your next meal. It is allowed to be uncomplicated.

start.speaker: npc
start.text: Airports feel unusually orderly to me. I started wondering why, and now my coffee has gone cold. What do you think makes a place feel safe?

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Maybe. Though an airport has unusual rules and unusual people passing through. How would we check the idea?

choices.text: Compare it with a similar busy place.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Good. One terminal and a hunch are not a finished theory.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: People who see it daily might notice things a traveler misses while guarding a croissant.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: That's interesting. A sign can sometimes do more than a warning. What would you borrow for city life?

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Yes. Being lost makes every small problem feel more threatening.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: A staffed place feels different from a silent system. I like that explanation, though I'll keep wondering.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Safe travels. I'll continue my research by finally drinking this coffee.

start.speaker: npc
start.text: A neighbor paid for a lovely public garden and treated the gardeners terribly. Someone says the donation settles the matter. Can generosity cancel cruelty?

choices.text: Both things should remain on the record.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: That feels right. We can enjoy the garden and still expect decent behavior. Who should get heard?

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Yes. Their experience isn't a rounding error in somebody else's generosity.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: A harder conversation than assigning one enormous moral score. Probably a more honest one.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: Certainly. I wouldn't uproot the flowers to prove a point. But how do we avoid selling permission to behave badly?

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: A thank-you can be sincere without becoming a pardon.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Exactly. A beautiful gesture is a beginning; how someone treats people tomorrow still counts.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: I hope you find both good company and a nice garden today.

ambient_031_a_diary_for_a_moving_world.title: A diary for a moving world
ambient_031_a_diary_for_a_moving_world.npc_voice: A little wistful, ready to begin

start.speaker: npc
start.text: I wish I'd recorded how I worked three years ago. Every little change felt normal, and now I can't reconstruct the old normal. What would you save from today?

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Yes! History keeps the grand events; someone should preserve the annoying login screen. What else belongs in the record?

choices.text: What people assume will never change.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Wonderful. A museum of misplaced certainty. I can contribute several exhibits.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: The hesitations, the shortcuts, the tea going cold. The details the big predictions always skip.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: That takes courage. Would you leave room to admit you were wrong?

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Then the diary can become a conversation with an earlier, overconfident version of you.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: A fine approach. Questions age gracefully, and they don't demand a victory parade.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Go make a small record of the day. Future you may be glad somebody noticed.

start.speaker: npc
start.text: I mentioned a country I'd visited and everyone asked about the food. The food was wonderful. I also met people who do things between meals. What would you ask about?

choices.text: Food can be a doorway into culture.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Good. The small customs can tell you so much. Which everyday thing interests you?

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: A lovely question. It gives you a place at the table without treating the table as the whole culture.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Yes! A joke can reveal a whole set of assumptions, including the ones you have just misunderstood.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: Absolutely. I just want to walk through the doorway. What question comes after 'was it tasty'?

choices.text: Who taught them to make it?
When do people eat it together?

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: Then we get a person, a family, maybe a history. Much more nourishing than a restaurant ranking.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Exactly. The occasion can matter as much as the ingredients.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: I hope your next journey comes with good questions and good lunch.

start.speaker: npc
start.text: I used to think a tidy recycling label meant the problem was solved. Now I want to follow the truck. Where would you start if you wanted less waste?

choices.text: Find out what actually gets recovered.
A well-managed landfill can have a role.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Yes. Paper, metals, plastics: different materials have different stories. What counts as success?

choices.text: Less material needed in the first place.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: A satisfying definition. The arrow on the bin should eventually point somewhere real.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Even better. Sometimes the best sorting process is not buying the third strainer.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: True. Keeping things contained may beat pretending they've vanished. What should happen next?

choices.text: Keep track of what is there.
Do not let that become an excuse to waste.

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: A slightly grim library, but perhaps a useful one for future recovery.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: Fair. 'Future archaeologists will enjoy this' is a poor defense of buying disposable everything.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Thanks for humoring my garbage questions. I promise they're carefully sorted.

ambient_034_the_house_with_a_thousand_ro.title: The house with a thousand rooms
ambient_034_the_house_with_a_thousand_ro.npc_voice: Excited by capability, wary of clutter

start.speaker: npc
start.text: AI helps me build software faster, so I keep adding features. My simple tool now resembles a house where every cupboard contains another staircase. What would you do?

choices.text: Decide what the thing is actually for.
More capability can justify more complexity.

a.speaker: npc
a.text: A rude but useful question. How would you draw the boundary?

choices.text: Pick the user's most important task.
Write down what I will not build.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Then a feature earns its room by making that task easier. The decorative staircase is nervous.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: A list of peaceful absences. I should frame it above the feature backlog.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: I agree. A workshop needs more tools than a picnic basket. What keeps it usable?

b1.speaker: npc
b1.text: So the complexity has an address instead of hiding behind every door.

b2.speaker: npc
b2.text: The most difficult feature request: fewer features. I'll ask for it while everyone is in a good mood.

leave.speaker: npc
leave.text: Good luck with whatever you're building. May its cupboards open normally.

start.speaker: npc
start.text: At twenty-three, I planned my life around equity that might pay out someday. Someday keeps rescheduling. What would you ask your younger self to consider?

choices.text: What can I enjoy or learn now?

a.speaker: npc
a.text: Yes. Some opportunities don't wait for a liquidity event. Which would you protect?

choices.text: Time with people I care about.
A chance to build useful skills.

a1.speaker: npc
a1.text: Hard to buy back later. A sensible thing to put on the calendar before the hypothetical millions.

a2.speaker: npc
a2.text: Something you can carry with you even if the shares never leave the spreadsheet.

b.speaker: npc
b.text: Certainly. I don't regret every long bet. What would make patience feel chosen rather than imposed?

choices.text: Knowing the terms and the risks.
Having some options along the way.

b1.speaker: npc
